candidates.claim_text: # Bags Split the Job: Mini Bags Catch the Eye, Large Bags Carry the Load
issues: The title states a general division of roles between mini and large bags that the Ledger does not establish across the market.
candidates.model_claim: # Bags Split the Job: Mini Bags Catch the Eye, Large Bags Carry the Load

candidates.claim_text: In 2026 fashion, mini bags are having a big moment.
issues: The cited coverage identifies a Fall 2026 styling direction, not a broad mini-bag moment throughout 2026 fashion.
candidates.model_claim: In 2026 fashion, mini bags are having a big moment.

candidates.claim_text: Palm-sized clutches, small pouches, and eye-catching minaudières fill runways and fashion reports.
issues: The Ledger gives selected examples, but does not establish that these forms fill runways and fashion reports broadly; “eye-catching” is also not stated for these examples.
candidates.model_claim: Palm-sized clutches, small pouches, and eye-catching minaudières fill runways and fashion reports.

candidates.claim_text: Some are so small that you might ask, “Can you really fit anything in that?”
issues: The Ledger describes limited essentials and a miniature book as possible contents, but does not establish that the bags are so small as to invite this question.
candidates.model_claim: Some are so small that you might ask, “Can you really fit anything in that?”

candidates.claim_text: But mini bags are not taking over.
issues: The Ledger warns that editorial visibility is not proof of market dominance, but does not establish the market-wide negative claim that mini bags are not taking over.
candidates.model_claim: But mini bags are not taking over.

candidates.claim_text: They are not pushing large bags away.
issues: Concurrent runway visibility does not directly establish that mini bags are not displacing large bags across the broader market.
candidates.model_claim: They are not pushing large bags away.

candidates.claim_text: In 2026, the two sizes seem to have different jobs.
issues: The role distinction is an article-level synthesis; the Ledger does not directly establish that the two sizes have different jobs across 2026 fashion.
candidates.model_claim: In 2026, the two sizes seem to have different jobs.

candidates.claim_text: One carries what we need.
issues: The Ledger gives examples of larger bags with practical capacity, but does not establish that large bags generally carry what people need.
candidates.model_claim: One carries what we need.

candidates.claim_text: They mostly hold the basics: a phone, wallet, keys, and lip products.
issues: ELLE's essentials explanation is not specifically attributed to the Khaite and Chanel examples, and the Ledger says “such as,” not that those examples mostly hold these items.
candidates.model_claim: They mostly hold the basics: a phone, wallet, keys, and lip products.

candidates.claim_text: They cannot compete with roomy bags for storage.
issues: The Ledger contrasts small bags' visual value with storage capacity, but does not directly compare them with roomy bags or say they cannot compete with them.
candidates.model_claim: They cannot compete with roomy bags for storage.

candidates.claim_text: They add a special feeling.
issues: The Ledger mentions occasion and visual impact, but does not say the bags add a special feeling.
candidates.model_claim: They add a special feeling.

candidates.claim_text: They say, “This is today’s mood.”
issues: The claim that the bags communicate a particular mood is not stated in the Ledger.
candidates.model_claim: They say, “This is today’s mood.”

candidates.claim_text: We see the season more clearly by looking at bags beside them.
issues: The Ledger does not state that looking at adjacent bags makes the season clearer; the sentence adds an unsupported interpretive relationship.
candidates.model_claim: We see the season more clearly by looking at bags beside them.

candidates.claim_text: It also showed Celine’s Ultra Maxi and Altuzarra’s large shoulder bag.
issues: The Ledger describes ultra-maxi proportions at Celine, but does not identify an item called “Celine’s Ultra Maxi.”
candidates.model_claim: It also showed Celine’s Ultra Maxi and Altuzarra’s large shoulder bag.

candidates.claim_text: This list matters.
issues: The assertion that the list matters is an evaluative claim not established by the Ledger.
candidates.model_claim: This list matters.

candidates.claim_text: Large bags had not disappeared.
issues: The Ledger documents large bags in selected coverage, but does not establish that large bags had not disappeared across the broader market.
candidates.model_claim: Large bags had not disappeared.

candidates.claim_text: We are not seeing mini bags spread through the whole market.
issues: The Ledger cautions against treating editorial visibility as proof of market-wide dominance, but does not establish that mini bags have not spread through the market.
candidates.model_claim: We are not seeing mini bags spread through the whole market.

candidates.claim_text: Instead, they are back in fashion reports and on certain runways.
issues: The Ledger documents mini bags in reports and selected shows, but does not establish that they are “back,” which implies a return after absence or decline.
candidates.model_claim: Instead, they are back in fashion reports and on certain runways.

candidates.claim_text: Even so, trends now look different.
issues: The claim that trends now look different implies a comparison with an earlier period that the Ledger does not establish.
candidates.model_claim: Even so, trends now look different.

candidates.claim_text: Bags no longer play a game with only one size on the throne.
issues: The Ledger supports simultaneous size visibility, but does not establish that bags previously had only one size dominant or that this has now changed.
candidates.model_claim: Bags no longer play a game with only one size on the throne.

candidates.claim_text: Large bags are the luggage crew.
issues: The Ledger supports functional examples of larger bags, but not the general characterization of large bags as a “luggage crew.”
candidates.model_claim: Large bags are the luggage crew.

candidates.claim_text: They carry what we need.
issues: Practical examples are documented, but the broad claim that large bags carry what people need is not established for the category as a whole.
candidates.model_claim: They carry what we need.

candidates.claim_text: Mini bags are the stage crew.
issues: ELLE describes visual impact for very small bags, but the sentence generalizes this role to mini bags as a category.
candidates.model_claim: Mini bags are the stage crew.

candidates.claim_text: They catch the eye and set the mood.
issues: Visual impact is supported for ELLE's editorial explanation, but setting the mood is not stated in the Ledger.
candidates.model_claim: They catch the eye and set the mood.

candidates.claim_text: In 2026, the runway proudly shows this split in their work.
issues: The Ledger shows small and large bags together on runways, but does not establish the claimed division of their roles or that the runway “proudly” shows it.
candidates.model_claim: In 2026, the runway proudly shows this split in their work.

candidates.claim_text: In 2026, large bags carry the load, while mini bags carry the mood.
issues: The summary asserts a general division in which large bags carry practical loads and mini bags carry mood, which the Ledger does not establish across the market.
candidates.model_claim: In 2026, large bags carry the load, while mini bags carry the mood.
